identity.name: Tsunami Hand-Wound Tourbillon
identity.one_liner: Hajime Asaoka's hand-made tourbillon in a 38mm titanium case — a single watchmaker in Yamanashi, Japan, with a movement that takes 200 hours to finish and an annual production under 12 pieces.

provenance_events.description: Hajime Asaoka releases the Tsunami, his first tourbillon — 38mm titanium case, hand-made movement with 200-hour finishing, 12 pieces a year.

narrative.story: Hajime Asaoka is a former boatbuilder who started making watches in 2009. The Tsunami is his most-photographed piece: a 38mm titanium case, a hand-made tourbillon movement with 200 hours of hand-finishing, a balance-wheel assembly that he builds from raw parts.
narrative.collector_notes: The Tsunami is unusual in that the tourbillon is on the dial side, not the back — you can see the tourbillon rotating through the dial.
